newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down but off low after Sakakibara comment.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down but off low after Sakakibara comment.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended lower on Thursday as the dollar rose sharply against the yen and Tokyo share prices jumped in reaction to comments by a senior Finance Ministry official.
JGBs finished off earlier lows, however, as investors bought cash bonds on dips, a brokerage house trader said.

"Investors were detected buying cash JGBs, mainly in the seven- to 10-year zones. There was talk that public funds were selling medium-term bonds and replacing them with long-term bonds," the trader said.
The September ended at 123.46, down from the previous day's close of 123.74. Turnover was 49,566 contracts.
It moved in a range of 123.25 to 123.83 during the day.
The key 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.430 percent as of 0625 GMT, up from Wednesday's close of 2.400 percent.
JGBs initially rose in the afternoon, after senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted as saying Japan's interest rates are unlikely to rise anytime soon.
But JGBs fell when Sakakibara was later quoted as saying a rise in rates over the medium-term can not be ruled out, traders said.
JGBs further extended losses, as the dollar soared to as high as 115.80 yen, after falling as low as 111.17 yen earlier in the day.
Traders said JGBs were also hurt by a rise in share prices which was triggered by the dollar's surge against the yen and active short-covering of banking sector issues.
Large-lot selling of JGB futures emerged against such a backdrop and accelerated the fall, the brokerage house trader said.
"Selling of JGB futures worth about 500 lots were detected and weighed on the market," he said.
Sakakibara, who spoke at a seminar held by the Japan Centre for International Finance on Thursday, was quoted by bankers attending the seminar as saying:
"It is unlikely that Japan's interest rates will be raised soon, given that the economic data for the April-June period will not be good."

Sakakibara was also quoted as saying Japan may have to wait until later this year before a decision is made on interest rates, and that he does not rule out a rise in Japan's interest rates in the medium-term.

In the cash bond market, the 140th to 149th JGBs were weak, after Wednesday's strength, while in contrast the 190th to 196th JGBs were strong, a trader for a foreign brokerage house said. This suggests that investors were replacing the former with the latter, he said.

The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd's debentures with four to five years to maturity were bought on Wednesday by pension funds, the trader added. The investors were attracted to the debentures' high yields relative to JGBs with similar maturities, and their high liquidity, he said.
